CIT-001.q: When does CIT Law 67/2025/QH15 take effect and from which tax period does it apply?
CIT-001.e: Law 67/2025/QH15 was passed on 14/6/2025, took effect on 01/10/2025 and applies from the 2025 CIT period.
CIT-001.x:
Basis: CIT Law 67/2025/QH15 (passed 14/06/2025).
Analysis: Effective 01/10/2025 but applied to the whole 2025 CIT period – so the 2025 finalisation follows the new law even though the old law governed the first nine months. This ties the change to the annual tax period.
Distractors: B confuses it with other tax laws (Law 149/2025); C is the VAT Law 48/2024 effective date; D is Decree 320/2025's effective date.

CIT-002.q: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP guiding the CIT Law takes effect:
o: From 15/12/2025 and applies to the 2025 CIT period
CIT-002.e: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP was issued and took effect on 15/12/2025, applying to the 2025 CIT period.
CIT-002.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP of 15/12/2025.
Analysis: Effective on issue and applied to the 2025 tax period, aligned with Law 67/2025. Consequence: 2025 finalisation must test deductibility under Decree 320 (with the transitional rule of Circular 20/2026 – see CIT-004).
Distractors: B, C and D have the wrong dates; 12/03/2026 is when Circular 20/2026 was issued.

CIT-003.q: The CIT circular replacing Circulars 78/2014/TT-BTC and 96/2015/TT-BTC is:
CIT-003.e: Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC (12/3/2026) guides Law 67/2025/QH15 and Decree 320/2025/ND-CP, replacing Circulars 78/2014, 96/2015 and the contractor-CIT part of Circular 103/2014.
CIT-003.x:
Basis: Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC of 12/03/2026.
Analysis: It guides Law 67/2025 and Decree 320/2025, replacing Circulars 78/2014 and 96/2015 and the CIT part of Circular 103/2014 on foreign contractors.
Distractors: Circular 89/2026 covers tax administration; Circular 99/2025 is the enterprise accounting regime; Circular 69/2025 isn't the CIT guidance.

CIT-004.q: For the 2025 tax period, Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC allows taxpayers to apply Circular 96/2015/TT-BTC guidance on conditions and documents for deductible expenses (except matters Circular 96 did not regulate).
CIT-004.e: True. This transitional rule avoids disruption to documentation for the 2025 finalisation.
CIT-004.x:
Basis: Transitional provisions of Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Since the Circular came in March 2026 – after 2025 ended – businesses may apply Circular 96/2015's guidance on deductibility conditions and records for 2025, except where Circular 96 was silent. This avoids retroactive documentation demands.
Note: Changes at Law/Decree level (e.g., the 20% interest cap, the 5 million threshold) still apply to 2025, as the transition only covers documentation guidance.

CIT-005.q: Select ALL CIT payers under Law 67/2025/QH15:
o: Enterprises established and operating under Vietnamese law
Foreign enterprises with a permanent establishment in Vietnam
Foreign enterprises without a PE but with taxable income arising in Vietnam
Foreign enterprises doing e-commerce or digital-platform business with income arising in Vietnam
CIT-005.e: Law 67/2025/QH15 and Decree 320/2025/ND-CP widen and clarify CIT payers, including foreign e-commerce/digital-platform businesses. Household businesses pay PIT, not CIT.
CIT-005.x:
Basis: Article 2 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: CIT taxpayers: (A) Vietnamese enterprises; (B) foreign enterprises with a permanent establishment in Vietnam; (C) foreign enterprises without one but with Vietnam-source income; (D) foreign e-commerce and digital platform businesses with income in Vietnam (clarified by the new law).
Distractors: (E) Household businesses aren't legal entities; their income is subject to PIT.

CIT-006.q: An organisation managing an e-commerce exchange or digital platform in Vietnam may have to pay tax on behalf of foreign enterprises in certain transactions under Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
CIT-006.e: True. Decree 320/2025/ND-CP provides for Vietnamese organisations (including e-commerce/digital platform operators) paying tax on behalf of foreign enterprises.
CIT-006.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. To capture income of foreign enterprises with no presence in Vietnam, Decree 320 makes certain Vietnamese organisations – including e-commerce and digital platform operators – withhold and pay CIT on their behalf.

CIT-007.q: The usual CIT tax period is:
o: The calendar year or the financial year
CIT-007.e: The CIT period is the calendar or financial year; some cases (e.g., foreign enterprises without a PE) are taxed per transaction.
CIT-007.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The CIT period is the calendar or financial year; businesses make quarterly provisional payments and finalise annually. Foreign enterprises without a permanent establishment are taxed per payment.
Distractors: B and C confuse provisional payment periods with the tax period; D applies only in special cases.

CIT-008.q: An enterprise may choose a financial year different from the calendar year (e.g., 01/4–31/3) and its CIT period follows that financial year.
CIT-008.e: True. The CIT period is the calendar year or the enterprise's financial year.
CIT-008.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Accounting Law 88/2015/QH13 (annual accounting period).
Analysis: True. Businesses with a non-calendar financial year (common in FDI firms following the parent) use that year as the tax period and must notify the tax authority.

CIT-009.q: An enterprise is established on 15/10/2026 with a calendar financial year. Its first CIT period may:
o: Be combined with 2027 into one period because 2026 is shorter than 3 months
Mandatorily cover only the 2.5 months of 2026
Be combined with the previous year
CIT-009.e: A first-year period shorter than 3 months is added to the next year's period; the total must not exceed 15 months.
CIT-009.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: 15/10–31/12/2026 is about 2.5 months (< 3 months), so it may be combined with 2027 into one tax period not exceeding 15 months (2.5 + 12 = 14.5).
Distractors: B – separate filing isn't mandatory; C – a combined return is still due; D – a new company has no prior year.

o: Taxable income minus exempt income and loss carried forward
CIT-010.e: Assessable income = taxable income − (exempt income + losses carried forward).
CIT-010.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Formula: Taxable income (thu nhập tính thuế) = assessable income − (exempt income + loss carried forward), then less any S&T fund appropriation before applying the rate.
Distractors: B and D ignore non-deductible adjustments and other income; C – accounting profit is only the starting point and must be adjusted.

o: Revenue minus deductible expenses, plus other income
CIT-011.e: Taxable income = revenue − deductible expenses + other income.
CIT-011.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Formula: Assessable income = revenue − deductible expenses + other income (including foreign income).
Analysis: In practice, the return starts from accounting profit before tax, adds back non-deductible expenses and subtracts downward adjustments (e.g., taxed dividends).
Distractors: B is after tax; C ignores expenses; D isn't income.

CIT-012.q: Select ALL items that are CIT-taxable income:
o: Income from disposal of fixed assets
Income from the first transfer after issuance of carbon credits by the enterprise granted them
CIT-012.e: Capital transfers, real estate, interest and asset disposals are taxable. The first transfer of carbon credits after issuance by the granted enterprise is exempt under Law 67/2025/QH15.
CIT-012.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15 (Articles 3 and 4); Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: (A) capital transfers, (B) property transfers, (C) deposit and loan interest, (D) fixed asset disposals are all assessable income.
Distractors: (E) Income from the first transfer of carbon credits after issuance by the issued enterprise is newly exempt (see CIT-036, CIT-040).

CIT-013.q: Select ALL items of other income subject to CIT:
o: Penalties and compensation received for a partner's breach of contract
Payables whose creditors cannot be identified
Income from selling scrap and rejects
CIT-013.e: Penalties/compensation received, payables with unidentified creditors and scrap sales are other income. Capital contributions and loans are not income.
CIT-013.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Taxable other income includes (A) penalties and compensation received; (B) payables with unidentifiable creditors (written back to income); (C) scrap sales.
Distractors: (D) Capital contributions are equity, not income; (E) loans are liabilities to be repaid, not income.

CIT-014.q: The time of recognising revenue for CIT on sales of goods is:
o: When ownership or the right to use goods passes to the buyer
When goods are dispatched to an agent
CIT-014.e: Revenue from sales of goods is recognised when ownership or the right to use passes to the buyer.
CIT-014.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Revenue from goods is recognised on transfer of ownership or right of use – consistent with the VAT tax point (Article 8 of Law 48/2024) and invoicing.
Distractors: B (payment) is cash basis, not applicable; C – signing doesn't transfer goods; D – consignment hasn't transferred ownership to the end buyer.

CIT-015.q: Revenue for CIT on goods sold on instalment or deferred payment is:
o: The one-off cash price, excluding instalment/deferred interest
CIT-015.e: Revenue is the one-off sale price; instalment/deferred interest is recognised as financial income over time.
CIT-015.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Instalment sales revenue is the one-off cash price; interest is recognised as financial income over time (consistent with VAS 14 and accruals). The treatment mirrors VAT (VAT-048).
Distractors: B uses cash flows; C is only interest; D is cost.

CIT-016.q: Income from a capital transfer by a Vietnamese enterprise is determined as:
o: Transfer price minus the purchase price of the transferred capital and transfer costs
Transfer price minus the company's charter capital
CIT-016.e: Capital transfer income = transfer price − purchase price of the capital − transfer costs.
CIT-016.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Formula: Capital gain = transfer price − purchase price of the transferred capital − transfer costs, added to assessable income at the company's rate.
Distractors: B taxes gross proceeds; C uses the investee's charter capital; D confuses it with the 0.1% PIT on securities or contractor tax.

CIT-017.q: Under Law 67/2025/QH15, a Vietnamese enterprise's taxable income arising abroad is declared in Vietnam, and foreign tax paid on that income is creditable as prescribed.
CIT-017.e: True. Vietnamese enterprises are taxed on foreign-source income and may credit foreign tax paid under the rules and tax treaties.
CIT-017.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; double taxation agreements.
Analysis: True. Vietnamese enterprises are taxed on worldwide income; foreign tax paid is credited but not beyond the Vietnamese CIT on that income.

CIT-018.e: The standard rate is 20%; 15% and 17% apply to small enterprises by annual revenue meeting conditions.
CIT-018.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The standard rate is 20%. 15% and 17% are size-based rates (CIT-019); some sectors have special rates (oil and gas, rare resources 25–50%).
Distractors: 15% and 17% apply only to eligible small firms; 22% was the rate before 2016.

CIT-019.q: Match total annual revenue with the CIT rate under Law 67/2025/QH15:
p: Over VND 3 billion up to VND 50 billion
Over VND 50 billion, or not eligible for 15%/17%
CIT-019.e: Law 67/2025/QH15 adds 15% and 17% rates for small enterprises based on total annual revenue.
CIT-019.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Annual revenue ≤ 3 billion → 15%; > 3 to ≤ 50 billion → 17%; > 50 billion or ineligible (e.g., related to an ineligible enterprise – CIT-023) → 20%.
Note: From 2026, enterprises with revenue ≤ 1 billion are also exempt (CIT-029).

CIT-020.q: Total annual revenue for determining the 15%/17% rates is based on:
o: Total revenue of the immediately preceding tax year (sales/services net of deductions, financial income, other income)
CIT-020.e: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP: based on prior-year total revenue, including sales/services revenue (excluding deductions), financial income and other income per the finalisation appendix.
CIT-020.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The revenue test uses the immediately preceding tax year, including sales and service revenue (net of deductions), financial income and other income per the finalisation appendix. Using the prior year lets businesses know their rate when paying quarterly.
Distractors: B and C are unstable and unverifiable; D – charter capital isn't a criterion.

CIT-021.q: Company A had total 2025 revenue of VND 3.5 billion and expects only VND 2 billion in 2026 (not excluded). Its rate for the 2026 period is:
CIT-021.e: The 15%/17% rate is determined from total revenue of the immediately preceding tax year.
CIT-021.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: 2025 revenue of 3.5 billion (> 3, ≤ 50 billion) → 17% for 2026, even if 2026 revenue drops to 2 billion. 2026 revenue will set the 2027 rate (15%).
Distractors: B and C use the wrong reference period; D – the rate isn't elective.

CIT-022.q: An enterprise established in April 2025 operated 9 months in 2025 with total revenue of VND 2.4 billion. What annualised revenue is used to determine its 2026 rate (VND)?
CIT-022.e: 2.4 billion / 9 × 12 = 3.2 billion VND; above 3 billion, so 17% applies in 2026 (if ≤ 50 billion and not excluded).
CIT-022.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: If the prior year was under 12 months, annualise: 2.4 billion / 9 × 12 = 3.2 billion. Being > 3 billion, 2026 uses 17% (if ≤ 50 billion and not excluded).
Note: Without annualising, the company would wrongly apply 15%.

CIT-023.q: A subsidiary of a large parent (annual revenue VND 2,000 billion) may still apply 15% if the subsidiary's own annual revenue does not exceed VND 3 billion.
CIT-023.e: False. 15%/17% do not apply to subsidiaries or related companies where a related enterprise does not meet the conditions.
CIT-023.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. The 15% and 17% rates target genuinely small firms; subsidiaries or related companies of ineligible enterprises can't use them – preventing groups from splitting into small units to get low rates.

CIT-024.q: Company A owns 30% of Company B (related). B's prior-year revenue was VND 2 billion; A's was VND 600 billion. B's CIT rate is:
CIT-024.e: B is related to an enterprise that does not meet the 15%/17% conditions, so 20% applies.
CIT-024.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Decree 132/2020/ND-CP (amended by Decree 20/2025/ND-CP) on related parties.
Analysis: A owns 30% of B (≥ 25% → related). A's revenue is 600 billion (> 50 billion), so it's ineligible for 15%/17% → B, despite only 2 billion revenue, applies 20%.
Distractors: A and B ignore the exclusion; D – 10% is a project incentive rate, irrelevant.

CIT-025.q: A newly established enterprise expects revenue not exceeding VND 3 billion and makes provisional payments at 15%. Actual year-end revenue is VND 4 billion. It must:
o: Re-determine the rate at 17% based on actual revenue, pay the shortfall and late-payment interest
CIT-025.e: New enterprises provisionally use expected revenue; at year-end they re-determine based on actual revenue and pay any shortfall plus late-payment interest.
CIT-025.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15 (late-payment interest).
Analysis: A new company provisionally uses forecast revenue; at finalisation, actual revenue of 4 billion (> 3 billion) means the correct rate is 17%. It must pay the 2-point difference plus late-payment interest on underpaid instalments.
Distractors: A keeps the wrong rate; C – 20% only if > 50 billion or excluded; D is backwards.

CIT-026.q: An enterprise with prior-year total revenue of VND 30 billion (not excluded) has 2026 assessable income of VND 2 billion and no incentives. What CIT is payable (VND)?
CIT-026.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Prior-year revenue 30 billion → 17%. CIT = 2,000,000,000 × 17% = 340,000,000 VND.
Note: Applying 20% would overpay 60 million.

CIT-027.q: An enterprise with prior-year total revenue of VND 2.5 billion (not excluded) has 2026 assessable income of VND 300 million. What CIT is payable (VND)?
CIT-027.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Prior-year revenue 2.5 billion (≤ 3 billion) → 15%. CIT = 300,000,000 × 15% = 45,000,000 VND.
Note: The 1 billion exemption (CIT-029) doesn't apply as revenue exceeds 1 billion.

CIT-028.q: An enterprise with prior-year total revenue of VND 12 billion (not excluded) has 2026 assessable income of VND 800 million. What CIT is payable (VND)?
CIT-028.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 11 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Prior-year revenue 12 billion → 17%. CIT = 800,000,000 × 17% = 136,000,000 VND.

CIT-029.q: From the 2026 tax period, enterprises and organisations established under Vietnamese law with total annual revenue of VND 1 billion or less are exempt from CIT.
CIT-029.e: True. Law 09/2026/QH16 added clause 14a to Article 4 of the CIT Law (threshold delegated to the Government); Decree 141/2026/ND-CP set it at VND 1 billion.
CIT-029.x:
Basis: Law 09/2026/QH16 adding Article 4(14a) of the CIT Law; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. From the 2026 period, Vietnamese enterprises and organisations with annual revenue of 1 billion or less are CIT-exempt – aligned with the household business threshold (VAT-009).
Note: Exemption doesn't remove accounting, invoicing or filing duties.

CIT-030.q: Under Decree 320/2025/ND-CP, for how long does the 10% incentive rate apply to certain income from new investment projects in incentivised sectors or areas?
CIT-030.e: The 10% incentive rate applies for 15 years; certain special projects may be extended.
CIT-030.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 18–20 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The 10% rate for 15 years applies to income from new projects in extremely disadvantaged areas, economic zones, high-tech zones, or specially encouraged sectors; some large high-tech projects get extensions. Time-limited exemptions/reductions also apply (e.g., 4 years exempt, 50% off for 9 years).
Distractors: 5, 10 and 20 years aren't the standard 10%-rate duration.

CIT-031.q: Select ALL groups of locations eligible for CIT incentives under Decree 320/2025/ND-CP:
o: Areas with extremely difficult socio-economic conditions
Economic zones, hi-tech parks, hi-tech agricultural zones, concentrated digital technology zones
Central districts of centrally governed cities
CIT-031.e: Three incentive location groups: extremely difficult; difficult; economic zones, hi-tech parks, hi-tech agricultural zones and concentrated digital technology zones.
CIT-031.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 18–20 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Three incentive location groups: (A) extremely disadvantaged; (B) disadvantaged; (C) economic zones, high-tech zones, high-tech agriculture zones and concentrated digital technology zones.
Distractors: (D) and (E) – large cities and central districts aren't incentive locations; location incentives aim at disadvantaged areas or special zones.

CIT-032.q: Select ALL agricultural activities on the CIT-incentivised list under Decree 320/2025/ND-CP:
o: Producing, multiplying and crossbreeding plant varieties and livestock breeds
Preserving agricultural, aquatic products and food
Producing and processing agricultural and aquatic products
CIT-032.e: The agricultural list includes forestry, breed production/multiplication, preservation and processing of agricultural and aquatic products (if conditions are met).
CIT-032.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 18–20 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Incentivised agriculture includes (A) afforestation and forest protection; (B) breeding and propagating plant varieties and livestock; (C) storage of farm, aquatic and food products; (D) farm and aquatic processing (subject to location/project conditions).
Distractors: (E) Resort real estate is property business and gets no sector incentive.

CIT-033.q: Select ALL technology activities on the CIT-incentivised list under Decree 320/2025/ND-CP:
o: Research, design, manufacture, packaging and testing of semiconductor chips
CIT-033.e: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP adds strategic technology sectors: semiconductors, AI data centres, software, information security…
CIT-033.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 18–20 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Decree 320 adds strategic technology sectors: (A) semiconductors (R&D, design, fabrication, packaging, testing); (B) AI data centres; (C) software and cybersecurity products.
Distractors: (D) Trading imported devices is commerce, not technology production; (E) pawn services aren't incentivised.

CIT-034.q: An enterprise whose business registration certificate lists an incentivised sector automatically enjoys CIT incentives.
CIT-034.e: False. Incentives depend on whether the investment project meets sector, location, project type and timing conditions, not the registered business line name.
CIT-034.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 18–20 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. Incentives attach to qualifying projects and their income (actual activity, location, scale, licensing/operation date), not registered business codes. Incentivised income must be accounted for separately.
Note: This is a common audit finding – wrongly claimed incentives are fully clawed back.

CIT-035.q: An enterprise already enjoying CIT incentives before Law 67/2025/QH15 took effect may choose to continue them for the remaining period or switch to the new incentives if it meets the conditions.
CIT-035.e: True. Transitional rules let enterprises choose the more suitable incentive if they meet the new law's conditions.
CIT-035.x:
Basis: Transitional provisions of Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Businesses enjoying incentives under the old law may keep them for the remaining period, or switch to the new law's incentives if eligible – protecting vested rights and investment stability.

CIT-036.q: Select ALL income newly added to CIT exemptions under Law 67/2025/QH15:
o: Income from the first transfer after issuance of emission-reduction certificates/carbon credits by the granted enterprise
Income from the first transfer of green bonds after issuance
CIT-036.e: Article 4(10) of Law 67/2025/QH15 exempts income relating to carbon credits and green bonds.
CIT-036.x:
Basis: Article 4(10) of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 4 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The new law adds exemptions to promote green finance: (A) first transfer of emission reduction certificates/carbon credits after issuance by the issued enterprise; (B) green bond interest; (C) first transfer of green bonds after issuance.
Distractors: (D) Ordinary deposit interest and (E) property transfers remain taxable.

CIT-037.q: Under Law 67/2025/QH15, the maximum exemption period for income from performing scientific research, technology development and innovation contracts, and from first sales of products made with technology newly applied in Vietnam, is:
CIT-037.e: Law 67/2025/QH15 shortened the maximum exemption from 5 years to 3 years.
CIT-037.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 4 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Income from R&D and innovation contracts, and products from technology first applied in Vietnam, is exempt for up to 3 years (old law: up to 5 years).
Distractors: 1 year is too short; 5 years is the old rule; 10 years has no basis.

CIT-038.q: Dividends and profits received from capital contributions to Vietnamese enterprises (which have paid CIT) are exempt income for the contributor.
CIT-038.e: True. Income from capital contributions/joint ventures with domestic enterprises, after the investee has paid CIT, is exempt.
CIT-038.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 4 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Profits were already taxed in the investee; exempting them at the investor avoids double taxation. In the return, such dividends are deducted as exempt income.
Note: Gains on selling the stake aren't dividends and remain taxable (CIT-016).

CIT-039.q: Grants received for scientific research and technology development are among the items Law 67/2025/QH15 added to exempt income.
CIT-039.e: True. Law 67/2025/QH15 added grants for scientific research, technology development and innovation to exempt income.
CIT-039.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 4 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Law 67/2025 adds grants received for scientific research, technology development and innovation to exempt income, provided they are used as intended.

CIT-040.q: Company X is granted carbon credits from a reforestation project and sells them for the first time; Company Y buys and resells them. Which income is CIT-exempt under Law 67/2025/QH15?
o: X's income from the first transfer after issuance
CIT-040.e: The exemption covers the first transfer after issuance by the granted enterprise; subsequent transfers are taxable.
CIT-040.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 4 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The exemption covers only the first transfer after issuance by the issued enterprise (X) – rewarding real emission reductions. Y's resale is credit trading and taxable.
Distractors: B and C extend the exemption to trading; D ignores the new exemption.

CIT-041.q: Select ALL CIT-exempt income (when conditions are met):
o: Income from cultivation, husbandry and agricultural processing by enterprises in extremely difficult areas
Income from technical services directly serving agriculture
Dividends from domestic enterprises that have paid CIT
Income from disposal of fixed assets
CIT-041.e: Agricultural income in extremely difficult areas, technical services for agriculture and domestic dividends are exempt; deposit interest and asset disposals are taxable.
CIT-041.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 4 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Exempt: (A) income from crops, livestock and farm processing in extremely disadvantaged areas; (B) technical services directly serving agriculture; (C) dividends from domestic companies that paid CIT.
Distractors: (D) Deposit interest and (E) asset disposals are taxable other income.

CIT-042.q: Select ALL conditions for an expense to be deductible for CIT:
o: Actually incurred and related to the enterprise's production/business
Supported by sufficient invoices and documents under the law
Purchases of VND 5 million or more per invoice (VAT-inclusive) must have non-cash payment documents, unless the Government provides otherwise
Approval by the Director is enough, no invoice needed
The expense must be within the annual budget approved by the Board
CIT-042.e: Three statutory conditions: actually incurred and business-related; sufficient invoices/documents; non-cash payment for invoices from VND 5 million. Internal approval or budgets do not replace tax-law conditions.
CIT-042.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Three statutory conditions: (A) actually incurred and business-related; (B) adequate invoices and documents; (C) invoices of 5 million or more (VAT-inclusive) paid by non-cash means (unless the Government provides otherwise).
Distractors: (D) Internal approval can't replace invoices; (E) a budget is a management tool, not a tax condition.

CIT-043.q: The invoice value from which purchases must have non-cash payment documents to be CIT-deductible under current rules is:
CIT-043.e: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP lowered the threshold from VND 20 million (Circular 96/2015/TT-BTC) to VND 5 million, aligned with the input VAT deduction condition under the 2024 VAT Law.
CIT-043.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The threshold fell from 20 million (Circular 96/2015) to 5 million (VAT-inclusive), aligned with the input VAT credit condition (VAT-070). One qualifying payment proof satisfies both taxes.
Distractors: B is the old threshold; C has the wrong amount and price basis; D has no basis.

CIT-044.q: A VND 30 million purchase invoice unpaid when the expense is recognised is still deductible; if it is later paid in cash, the enterprise must reduce expenses correspondingly in the tax period of payment.
CIT-044.e: True. Unpaid expenses are provisionally deductible; if paid in cash (failing the non-cash condition), reduce expenses in the period of payment.
CIT-044.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Unpaid purchases are deductible on accrual; if later paid in cash (failing the condition), the expense is reduced in the period of payment – mirroring the input VAT adjustment (VAT-073).

CIT-045.q: An employee authorised under the company's financial regulations pays VND 8 million of business-trip costs with a personal bank card (invoice in the company's name); the company then reimburses the employee by transfer. The expense is deductible.
CIT-045.e: True. Where an authorised employee pays non-cash, invoices/documents are sufficient, the authorisation is in the enterprise's regulations or decision, and the enterprise reimburses the employee, the expense is deductible.
CIT-045.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Four conditions: (1) a financial policy or authorisation decision; (2) the employee pays non-cash (personal card); (3) the invoice is in the company's name; (4) the company reimburses by transfer.
Note: Cash reimbursement breaks the non-cash chain (VAT-075).

CIT-046.q: Interest on loans from individuals or non-credit-institution organisations for production/business is deductible up to which rate?
o: The maximum rate under the Civil Code (20%/year)
150% of the SBV base rate at the time of borrowing
The 12-month deposit rate of state commercial banks
Unlimited if there is a loan contract
CIT-046.e: Law 67/2025/QH15 replaces the 150%-of-base-rate cap with the Civil Code rate (max 20%/year). The excess is non-deductible.
CIT-046.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 468 of the 2015 Civil Code.
Analysis: For loans from non-credit institutions, deductible interest can't exceed the Civil Code maximum – 20%/year; the excess is non-deductible.
Distractors: B is the old cap (150% of the base rate); C has no basis; D ignores the statutory limit.
Note: Related-party interest is also capped at 30% of EBITDA under Decree 132/2020 (amended by Decree 20/2025).

CIT-047.q: A company borrows VND 3 billion from an individual for all of 2026 at 24%/year to buy raw materials. How much interest is NOT deductible for 2026 CIT (VND)?
CIT-047.e: Interest payable: 3 billion × 24% = 720 million; deductible: 3 billion × 20% = 600 million; the excess 120,000,000 VND is non-deductible.
CIT-047.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Article 468 of the 2015 Civil Code.
Working: Interest paid = 3 billion × 24% = 720 million. Deductible = 3 billion × 20% = 600 million. Non-deductible = 720 − 600 = 120,000,000 VND.
Note: The company must also withhold 5% PIT on interest paid to the individual lender.

CIT-048.q: Interest on loans corresponding to charter capital not yet contributed per the charter's contribution schedule is not deductible.
CIT-048.e: True. Interest corresponding to unpaid charter capital is non-deductible.
CIT-048.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. When owners haven't contributed charter capital on schedule, borrowing that fills the gap substitutes for equity; the related interest is non-deductible, typically computed as interest × (unpaid capital / total borrowings) over the shortfall period.

CIT-049.q: Select ALL expenses that are NOT deductible:
o: Administrative fines for tax, traffic and environmental violations
Depreciation of a car used privately by the Director, not for business
Production machinery maintenance with invoices paid by transfer
Wages paid to employees under labour contracts and the pay policy
CIT-049.e: Administrative fines (including late-payment interest) and depreciation of assets not used for business are non-deductible. Documented maintenance costs and wages are deductible.
CIT-049.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Non-deductible: (A) administrative fines; (B) late-payment interest on tax; (C) depreciation of assets not used for business (a car for personal use).
Distractors: (D) Machine maintenance with invoices and transfer, and (E) wages under contracts and policies, meet the general conditions and are deductible.

CIT-050.q: Penalties for breach of commercial contracts paid to partners (with contract, minutes, documents) are administrative fines and therefore non-deductible.
CIT-050.e: False. Contractual penalties are not administrative fines; with full documentation and a business link they may be deductible.
CIT-050.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. Contract penalties are civil/commercial sanctions by agreement, unlike administrative fines imposed by the State. With a contract, minutes, documents and business relevance, they can be deductible.

CIT-051.q: Welfare expenses directly for employees (weddings/funerals, holidays, medical and study support…) are deductible up to a total of:
o: One month of the actual average salary paid in the tax year
Two months of the actual average salary
CIT-051.e: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP keeps the cap on total welfare expenses at one month of the actual average salary in the tax year.
CIT-051.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Total direct welfare spending for employees (weddings/funerals, holidays, medical and study support, hardship…) is deductible up to one month of average actual salary for the year (actual payroll / months of operation).
Distractors: B doubles the cap; C and D have no basis.

CIT-052.q: In 2026 a company's actual payroll is VND 6 billion (12 months). Total welfare spending (holidays, weddings/funerals, hardship support) is VND 650 million, fully documented. How much welfare spending is NOT deductible (VND)?
CIT-052.e: Average monthly salary = 6 billion / 12 = 500 million; deductible cap 500 million; excess 650 − 500 = 150,000,000 VND.
CIT-052.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Average monthly salary = 6 billion / 12 = 500 million = the welfare cap. Non-deductible excess = 650 − 500 = 150,000,000 VND.
Note: Use actual salaries paid in the year, not planned payroll.

CIT-053.q: Advertising, promotion, marketing, conference and entertainment expenses are capped at 15% of total deductible expenses.
CIT-053.e: False. The 15% cap was abolished from the 2015 tax period and is not reinstated by Law 67/2025/QH15; such expenses are deductible if general conditions are met.
CIT-053.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. The 15% cap on advertising, marketing, promotion and entertainment was abolished from the 2015 period (Law 71/2014/QH13), and Law 67/2025 didn't reinstate it. These expenses are deductible under the general conditions.
Note: Entertainment spending is still scrutinised for business relevance.

CIT-054.q: Under Decree 320/2025/ND-CP, actual R&D expenses (meeting conditions) are deductible up to 200% of actual cost, provided the enterprise does not incur a loss after the deduction.
CIT-054.e: True. The additional deduction does not apply to costs funded by other sources or spent from the enterprise's science and technology development fund.
CIT-054.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Qualifying R&D is deductible up to 200% of actual cost (an extra 100% 'super deduction'), provided the business isn't in a loss afterwards; it doesn't apply to costs funded from other sources or the S&T fund (no double benefit).

CIT-055.q: Select ALL expenses Law 67/2025/QH15 adds or clarifies as deductible:
o: Support for building public infrastructure that also serves the enterprise's business
Costs of greenhouse-gas emission reduction linked to business
Contributions to funds established by the Government or Prime Minister
CIT-055.e: Law 67/2025/QH15 expands deductions: extra R&D, public infrastructure support also serving the business, GHG reduction, contributions to Government/PM funds. Late-payment interest and excess interest remain non-deductible.
CIT-055.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Law 67/2025 adds or clarifies deductible items: (A) additional R&D deduction; (B) support for public infrastructure also serving the business; (C) greenhouse gas reduction costs tied to operations; (D) contributions to funds established by the Government or Prime Minister.
Distractors: (E) Late-payment interest and (F) individual loan interest above 20%/year remain non-deductible (CIT-046, CIT-049).

CIT-056.q: A textile-dyeing plant invests in wastewater treatment and heat recovery to cut emissions. Operating costs linked to production are deductible when invoice/document conditions are met.
CIT-056.e: True. GHG emission-reduction costs linked to business are deductible under Law 67/2025/QH15.
CIT-056.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Operating costs of wastewater treatment and heat recovery are both environmental obligations and emission reductions directly tied to production; deductible with proper invoices and payment. The capital outlay is capitalised and deducted via depreciation.

CIT-057.q: An agri-processing company buys green coffee directly from farming households selling their own produce (no invoices). The documents for the expense to be deductible are:
o: A purchase list (form 02/TNDN) signed by the legal representative or authorised person; non-cash payment if VND 5 million or more per day per person
Farmers must register a business and issue invoices
Just a cash voucher signed by the seller
CIT-057.e: Purchases of agricultural products from direct producers may use a purchase list instead of invoices; payments of VND 5 million or more per day per person must be non-cash.
CIT-057.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Purchases of farm produce from producers (no invoice) use a Purchase List (Form 02/TNDN) signed by the legal representative or authorised person, who vouches for its truthfulness. Payments of 5 million or more per day per seller must be non-cash.
Distractors: B – self-producing farmers needn't register a business; C lacks the list and breaches the payment condition at 5 million or more; D is too strict.
Note: Keep the seller's ID, weighing slips and farm address to prove substance.

CIT-058.q: Wages accrued as expenses in the period but not actually paid or without payment documents are not deductible.
CIT-058.e: True. Wage expenses must actually be paid and documented.
CIT-058.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Salary expense must be actually paid with payment evidence (signed payroll, transfer records). Accrued but unpaid salaries at filing are deductible only within the prescribed salary reserve and must be paid within the allowed time.

CIT-059.q: Part of the inventory is damaged by flooding; the loss is VND 500 million and insurance compensates VND 320 million. Documentation is complete. How much of the loss is deductible (VND)?
CIT-059.e: Only the uncompensated portion of losses from natural disasters/epidemics is deductible: 500 − 320 = 180,000,000 VND.
CIT-059.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Disaster loss = 500 million; insurance recovery = 320 million. Deductible = unrecovered loss = 500 − 320 = 180,000,000 VND.
Note: Keep stock-count minutes, loss valuation and insurance claim documents.

CIT-060.q: Sponsorships for education, healthcare, disaster relief and charity housing with the required confirmation documents are deductible.
CIT-060.e: True. Sponsorships to the right beneficiaries with required documents are deductible.
CIT-060.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Sponsorships for education, health, disaster relief, charity housing, etc. are deductible when to eligible recipients with documentation: a sponsorship confirmation signed by both parties and transfer records.

CIT-061.q: Accrued periodic expenses (e.g., major repairs) not spent or not fully spent by the end of the period: the unspent portion is not deductible.
CIT-061.e: True. Unspent accruals must be reversed from expenses.
CIT-061.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Accruals must be settled against actual spend; any excess at the end of the term is reversed. This prevents using accruals to shift profit between years.

CIT-062.q: Deducted input VAT and CIT expense are not deductible expenses.
CIT-062.e: True. These are excluded when determining taxable income.
CIT-062.x:
Basis: Article 9 of Law 67/2025/QH15; Articles 9 and 10 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Credited input VAT isn't an expense (VAT-080); CIT expense is a distribution of profit and deducting it would be circular. Both are excluded from assessable income calculations.

CIT-063.q: Trade-union fees paid by the enterprise at 2% of the payroll used for social-insurance contributions are deductible.
CIT-063.e: True. Statutory trade-union fees are deductible.
CIT-063.x:
Basis: Trade Union Law 50/2024/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The 2% trade union fee on the social insurance salary base is a statutory employer obligation, deductible with payment evidence – like the employer's social, health and unemployment insurance contributions.

CIT-064.q: The maximum loss carry-forward period for CIT is:
o: No more than 5 consecutive years from the year after the loss
CIT-064.e: Losses are carried forward continuously and in full to subsequent years' assessable income for up to 5 years from the year after the loss.
CIT-064.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Tax losses are carried forward continuously and in full for up to 5 years from the year after the loss; any balance beyond that lapses.
Distractors: 3 years, 10 years or unlimited don't reflect Vietnamese law (some other countries allow unlimited carry-forward).

CIT-065.q: In 2024 a company had a tax loss of VND 600 million. In 2025 taxable income was VND 250 million, fully offset by losses. In 2026 taxable income is VND 1,100 million, with no exempt income and no S&T fund. What is 2026 assessable income (VND)?
CIT-065.e: Remaining loss after 2025: 600 − 250 = 350 million (within 5 years). 2026 assessable income = 1,100 − 350 = 750,000,000 VND.
CIT-065.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: 2024 loss = 600 million; 250 million used in 2025 → 350 million left (valid until 2029). 2026 taxable income = 1,100 − 350 = 750,000,000 VND.
Note: Carry-forward is 'continuous and in full' – losses can't be saved for a higher-rate year.

CIT-066.q: Losses from real-estate transfers may be offset against income from other business activities, except income enjoying CIT incentives.
CIT-066.e: True. Law 67/2025/QH15 lets enterprises decide to offset losses from real-estate and investment-project transfers against other business income (excluding incentivised activities).
CIT-066.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The new law allows offsetting losses from property and project transfers against other business income – previously property had to be ring-fenced. Exception: no offset against incentivised income (to preserve the incentive's intent).

CIT-067.q: Losses from transferring mineral exploration, extraction and processing projects may be offset against other business income.
CIT-067.e: False. Income from transferring mineral exploration, extraction and processing projects must be declared and taxed separately, not offset.
CIT-067.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. Transfers of mineral exploration, extraction and processing projects are still ring-fenced and taxed separately, with no offset against other activities – reflecting the resource nature and special rates of this sector.

CIT-068.q: The loss carried forward is the negative taxable income determined under tax law, not the accounting loss in the financial statements.
CIT-068.e: True. Tax losses may differ from accounting losses due to adjustments (non-deductible expenses, exempt income…).
CIT-068.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. The carried-forward loss is the tax loss on the return (after adding back non-deductibles, removing exempt income…), not the accounting loss. E.g., an accounting loss of 500 million with 200 million non-deductible gives a tax loss of only 300 million.

CIT-069.q: Under Decree 320/2025/ND-CP, what maximum percentage of annual assessable income may an enterprise set aside for its Science and Technology Development Fund?
CIT-069.e: The cap was raised from 10% to 20% of annual assessable income, before calculating CIT.
CIT-069.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: The S&T fund appropriation cap rose from 10% to 20% of annual taxable income, deducted before tax. The fund must be used properly within the prescribed time; misuse or underuse requires repaying the tax plus interest.
Distractors: 10% is the old cap; 15% and 30% have no basis.

CIT-070.q: A company has 2026 assessable income of VND 2 billion, rate 20%, and sets aside the maximum S&T Development Fund. What CIT is payable (VND)?
CIT-070.e: Maximum fund: 20% × 2 billion = 400 million. CIT = (2,000 − 400) million × 20% = 320,000,000 VND.
CIT-070.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Maximum appropriation = 20% × 2 billion = 400 million. Taxable income after appropriation = 2,000 − 400 = 1,600 million. CIT = 1,600 × 20% = 320,000,000 VND (80 million less than without it).
Note: It is a conditional deferral – if unused on time, the tax is repaid with interest.

CIT-071.q: Within 5 years of setting aside the S&T Fund, if it is unused, less than 70% is used, or it is misused, the enterprise must pay CIT on the corresponding amount set aside plus interest.
CIT-071.e: True. This claws back the incentive when the fund is not used properly or sufficiently.
CIT-071.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP (S&T development fund).
Analysis: True. The appropriation is a conditional incentive: at least 70% must be used properly within 5 years. Breaches (unused, under 70%, misuse) trigger CIT on the relevant portion plus interest.
Note: Track each appropriation and each fund outlay separately to prove the usage ratio.

CIT-072.q: Expenses paid from the enterprise's S&T Development Fund are again deductible when determining taxable income.
CIT-072.e: False. Spending funded by the fund (already deducted when set aside) cannot be deducted twice.
CIT-072.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. The appropriation was already deducted before tax; deducting fund outlays again would double count. So spending from the fund isn't deductible (nor eligible for the additional R&D deduction – CIT-054).

CIT-073.q: Fixed assets formed from the S&T Fund that are transferred to business use before being fully depreciated: the remaining value is included in other income and depreciation continues as a deductible expense.
CIT-073.e: True. Decree 320/2025/ND-CP guides the treatment of fund-financed assets when their use changes.
CIT-073.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. If an asset funded by the (already tax-deducted) fund is redeployed to ordinary business, the incentive no longer fits; its residual value is added to other income, and the asset continues to be depreciated as a deductible expense – neutralising the benefit overall.

CIT-074.q: Under Decree 252/2026/ND-CP, the deadline for quarterly provisional CIT payment is:
o: The last day of the first month of the following quarter
The 20th of the first month of the following quarter
The last day of the quarter in which the obligation arises
The 30th of the third month of the following quarter
CIT-074.e: Article 24 of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP: provisional quarterly payment is due by the last day of the first month of the following quarter (previously the 30th of that month).
CIT-074.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 24 of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Quarterly CIT is due by the last day of the first month of the next quarter (e.g., Q3 → 31/10). The old rule (Decree 126/2020) was the 30th – a small change that matters in 31-day months.
Distractors: B (the 20th) is the monthly filing deadline; C and D are wrong.

CIT-075.q: The Q3/2026 provisional CIT deadline falls on Saturday 31/10/2026. The last day to pay without late-payment interest is:
CIT-075.e: When the last day of a deadline is a day off, the deadline ends on the next working day: Monday 02/11/2026.
CIT-075.x:
Basis: Article 24 of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP; Article 148 of the 2015 Civil Code.
Analysis: 31/10/2026 is a Saturday. When a deadline falls on a day off, it ends on the next working day – Monday 02/11/2026, with no late-payment interest.
Distractors: B – paying early isn't required; C contradicts the Civil Code; D is late.

CIT-076.q: Enterprises do not file quarterly provisional CIT returns; they self-determine and pay provisionally, and the obligation is finalised annually.
CIT-076.e: True. CIT is paid provisionally each quarter without quarterly returns, and finalised annually.
CIT-076.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 24 of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. There is no quarterly CIT return; businesses estimate and pay provisionally, then finalise annually. The safeguard is the 80% minimum (CIT-077).

CIT-077.q: Total provisional CIT paid over 4 quarters must be at least 80% of the CIT finalised for the year; otherwise late-payment interest applies to the shortfall.
CIT-077.e: True. Article 24(3) of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP keeps the 80% minimum.
CIT-077.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 24(3) of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Four quarterly payments must reach at least 80% of the final CIT. The shortfall against 80% bears interest from after the Q4 deadline; the remaining 20% is due with the finalisation without interest.

CIT-078.q: 2026 finalised CIT is VND 500 million; provisional payments over 4 quarters total VND 300 million. On what amount is late-payment interest charged (the shortfall against 80%) (VND)?
CIT-078.e: 80% × 500 = 400 million; shortfall 400 − 300 = 100,000,000 VND bears late-payment interest from the day after the Q4 provisional deadline. The other 100 million is due with the finalisation.
CIT-078.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 24 of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Minimum = 80% × 500 = 400 million. Paid 300 → shortfall 100 million bears interest from after the Q4 deadline. The other 100 million (500 − 400) is due at finalisation without interest.
Note: The question asks for the interest-bearing part, not the total balance due (200 million).

CIT-079.q: An enterprise estimates full-year 2026 CIT at VND 400 million and has paid VND 260 million for the first three quarters. What is the minimum Q4 provisional payment to reach 80% (VND)?
CIT-079.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 24 of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 80% × 400 = 320 million; paid 260 → Q4 minimum = 320 − 260 = 60,000,000 VND.
Note: Pay above the minimum when Q4 profit is hard to forecast.

CIT-080.q: Late-payment interest on provisional CIT below the 80% minimum is calculated from:
o: The day after the Q4 provisional deadline to the day before the shortfall is paid
The day after the annual finalisation filing deadline
The first day of the tax year
The date the tax authority issues an audit decision
CIT-080.e: The shortfall against 80% bears interest from the day after the Q4 provisional payment deadline.
CIT-080.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Article 24 of Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Interest on the shortfall against 80% runs from the day after the Q4 provisional deadline to the day before the shortfall is paid.
Distractors: B shortens the period; C and D aren't linked to provisional payments.

CIT-081.q: The late-payment interest rate under the 2025 Tax Administration Law is:
o: 0.03% per day on the late tax amount
CIT-081.e: Law 108/2025/QH15 keeps 0.03% per day on the late tax amount.
CIT-081.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Late-payment interest of 0.03%/day on the overdue tax (about 10.95%/year) is retained from Law 38/2019.
Distractors: 0.05%/day was the pre-2016 rate; 0.07%/day and 1%/month aren't current.

CIT-082.q: An enterprise pays VND 200 million of CIT 20 days late. What is the late-payment interest (VND)?
CIT-082.x:
Basis: Tax Administration Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP Art. 24 (per the question) – late interest at 0.03% a day.
Working: Late interest = 200,000,000 × 0.03% × 20 days = 60,000 × 20 = 1,200,000 VND.
Analysis: 0.03% a day ≈ 10.95% a year. Firms whose quarterly CIT prepayments fall more than 20% short of the final liability also owe late interest on the shortfall from the Q4 deadline. Late interest isn't CIT-deductible.
Note: Decree 252/2026 is a 2026 text beyond my knowledge; check the original.

CIT-083.q: An enterprise has a calendar financial year. The deadline for its 2026 CIT finalisation return is:
CIT-083.e: The last day of the third month after year-end: 31/3/2027 (next working day if it falls on a day off).
CIT-083.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: The CIT finalisation is due by the last day of the third month after year-end → 31/03/2027, with payment the same day; a day off shifts it to the next working day.
Distractors: B is the PIT self-finalisation deadline for individuals; C is the Q4 provisional deadline; D has no basis.

CIT-084.q: An enterprise's financial year runs 01/4 to 31/3. The finalisation deadline for the year ending 31/3/2027 is:
CIT-084.e: The last day of the third month after the year-end (31/3/2027) is 30/6/2027.
CIT-084.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Year ends 31/03/2027 → the third month after is June 2027 → due 30/06/2027.
Distractors: B is the year-end date; C and D miscount months.

CIT-085.q: Match each account under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC with what it records:
CIT-085.e: CIT accounts under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (replacing Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC from 01/01/2026).
CIT-085.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC (enterprise accounting regime, from 01/01/2026).
Analysis: 3334 – CIT payable; 8211 – current tax expense; 8212 – deferred tax expense; 243 – deferred tax assets; 347 – deferred tax liabilities. The structure carries over from Circular 200/2014 and follows VAS 17.

CIT-086.q: Under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC, top-up CIT expense under global minimum tax rules is recorded in account 82112.
CIT-086.e: True. Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC adds account 82112 for top-up CIT under global minimum tax rules.
CIT-086.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; Resolution 107/2023/QH15 on the global minimum tax.
Analysis: True. Members of multinational groups with revenue of at least EUR 750 million may owe top-up CIT (QDMTT) to reach a 15% effective rate; Circular 99 adds account 82112 to record this separately.

CIT-087.q: When total provisional CIT exceeds the annual finalised amount, the overpayment is offset against other tax obligations or refunded under tax administration law.
CIT-087.e: True. Taxpayers may offset or claim refunds of overpaid tax.
CIT-087.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Provisional payments above the final liability are overpayments; they can be offset against later or other taxes, or refunded under tax procedures.

CIT-088.q: 2026 accounting profit before tax is VND 1,500 million, including VND 150 million dividends from a domestic joint-stock company (which paid CIT). No other adjustments; rate 20%. What CIT is payable (VND)?
CIT-088.e: Dividends are exempt: assessable income = 1,500 − 150 = 1,350 million; CIT = 1,350 × 20% = 270,000,000 VND.
CIT-088.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Dividends from tax-paid domestic companies are exempt → taxable income = 1,500 − 150 = 1,350 million; CIT = 1,350 × 20% = 270,000,000 VND.
Note: Taxing 1,500 million (300 million) would double-tax the dividends.

CIT-089.q: Accounting profit before tax is VND 2,000 million. Expenses include administrative fines of 50 million and excess individual-loan interest of 120 million. Income includes domestic dividends of 300 million. Rate 20%, no losses. What CIT is payable (VND)?
CIT-089.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Add back non-deductibles: fines 50 + excess interest 120 = 170 million. Deduct exempt dividends 300 million. Taxable income = 2,000 + 170 − 300 = 1,870 million; CIT = 374,000,000 VND.

CIT-090.q: Company A (20% rate) sells its entire capital in Company B for VND 5.2 billion; the purchase price was VND 3.5 billion; no transfer costs. What CIT arises on this income (VND)?
CIT-090.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Capital gain = 5.2 − 3.5 − 0 = 1.7 billion; CIT = 1.7 billion × 20% = 340,000,000 VND.
Note: Keep the contract and purchase cost evidence to avoid a deemed price assessment.

CIT-091.q: Accounting profit before tax is VND 900 million; depreciation of assets not used for business is VND 90 million; prior-year loss carried forward is VND 200 million. Rate 20%. What CIT is payable (VND)?
CIT-091.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Assessable income = 900 + 90 (non-deductible depreciation) = 990 million; less 200 loss → 790 million; CIT = 790 × 20% = 158,000,000 VND.

CIT-092.q: A company had total 2025 revenue of VND 40 billion (not excluded). In 2026: accounting profit before tax VND 1,000 million; non-deductible expenses VND 100 million; exempt income VND 50 million. What is 2026 CIT (VND)?
CIT-092.e: Prior-year revenue over 3 up to 50 billion → 17%. Assessable income = 1,000 + 100 − 50 = 1,050 million; CIT = 1,050 × 17% = 178,500,000 VND.
CIT-092.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Working: Prior-year revenue 40 billion (> 3, ≤ 50 billion) → 17%. Taxable income = 1,000 + 100 − 50 = 1,050 million; CIT = 178,500,000 VND.
Note: Determine the rate first from prior-year revenue.

CIT-093.q: Arrange the steps to determine CIT payable for the year:
o: Make upward/downward adjustments to reach taxable income
Deduct exempt income and losses carried forward to reach assessable income
Deduct the S&T Fund appropriation (if any)
Deduct exemptions/reductions and creditable foreign tax (if any)
CIT-093.e: CIT payable = (assessable income − S&T Fund) × rate; then deduct exemptions/reductions and creditable foreign tax.
CIT-093.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: (1) Accounting profit → (2) adjustments to assessable income → (3) less exempt income and losses to taxable income → (4) less S&T fund → (5) apply the rate → (6) less exemptions/reductions and foreign tax credits.
Note: Swapping (3) and (4) misstates the fund, which is based on taxable income.

CIT-094.q: Income from capital transfers and real-estate transfers (other than social housing) of an enterprise enjoying incentives also benefits from the project's incentive rate, exemptions and reductions.
CIT-094.e: False. CIT incentives do not apply to income from capital transfers, real-estate transfers (except social housing) and certain other income.
CIT-094.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: False. Incentives attach to income from the incentivised project; capital and property transfer income (except social housing) and other unrelated income are taxed at normal rates.

CIT-095.q: Mark True/False for each CIT statement:
o: Dividends from a domestic company that paid CIT are excluded from assessable income
Late-payment interest on tax is deductible
Tax losses can be carried forward for up to 5 consecutive years
Individual-loan interest at 18%/year with a contract and bank transfer documents is fully deductible
CIT-095.e: Domestic dividends are exempt; late-payment interest is non-deductible; losses carry forward up to 5 years; 18%/year does not exceed the Civil Code's 20%/year cap so it is deductible.
CIT-095.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; 2015 Civil Code.
Analysis: (1) True – domestic dividends are exempt. (2) False – late-payment interest isn't deductible. (3) True – losses carry forward up to 5 consecutive years. (4) True – 18%/year ≤ 20%/year, with a contract and transfer records, so fully deductible.

CIT-096.q: Export furniture manufacturer – select ALL expenses that ARE deductible (with full invoices/documents and proper payment):
o: Plantation timber bought from self-growing households, with a purchase list in the prescribed form and paid by transfer
Fire prevention and protective equipment for the workshop
Depreciation of factory buildings and machinery in use
Depreciation of the owner's resort villa not used for business
CIT-096.e: Materials bought from self-producers with a purchase list, safety costs and depreciation of business assets are deductible; administrative fines and depreciation of non-business assets are not.
CIT-096.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Deductible: (A) plantation timber bought from growers – Form 02/TNDN and transfer; (B) fire safety and protective equipment; (C) depreciation of assets in use.
Distractors: (D) Environmental administrative fines aren't deductible; (E) the owner's villa doesn't serve the business – its depreciation isn't deductible.

CIT-097.q: Under Resolution 198/2025/QH15, small and medium enterprises are exempt from CIT for 3 years from the date of their first business registration certificate.
CIT-097.e: True. This is the private-sector support policy in Article 10 of Resolution 198/2025/QH15.
CIT-097.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Resolution 198/2025/QH15 on private sector development.
Analysis: True. SMEs are CIT-exempt for 3 years from their first enterprise registration certificate. Note the 'first' condition – entities formed by splitting or converting existing businesses may not qualify.

CIT-098.q: CIT revenue from providing services is determined at:
o: Completion of the service or of each part of the service for the buyer
CIT-098.e: Service revenue is recognised on completion of the service or each part; if invoiced earlier, at invoicing.
CIT-098.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Service revenue is recognised on completion or partial completion; if invoiced earlier, at invoicing – consistent with the VAT tax point.
Distractors: B (advance), C (signing) and D (full payment) aren't accrual triggers.

CIT-099.q: CIT revenue of an enterprise using the VAT credit method is revenue excluding VAT.
CIT-099.e: True. Credit-method VAT payers determine CIT revenue excluding VAT.
CIT-099.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Under the credit method, output VAT is collected for the State, not revenue; CIT revenue excludes VAT. Under the direct method, revenue includes VAT.

CIT-100.q: An enterprise leases out a cold store and receives 3 years' rent in advance. Revenue for CIT is determined by:
o: Allocation over the prepaid years or recognition as one-off revenue (the enterprise chooses)
Mandatory full recognition in the year of receipt
Recognition only at the end of the contract
No tax because it is an advance
CIT-100.e: Where the lessee prepays for several years, taxable revenue is allocated over the prepaid years or recognised as one-off revenue.
CIT-100.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: For multi-year prepaid rent, the business may spread taxable revenue over the prepaid years or recognise it at once. Lump-sum recognition can help during a tax holiday.
Distractors: B is too strict; C and D have no basis.
Note: Unlike VAT, which is due on the full prepayment at receipt (VAT-134).

CIT-101.q: Under Decree 141/2026/ND-CP, the total annual revenue used to test the CIT exemption for enterprises with revenue of VND 1 billion or less is based on:
CIT-101.e: Based on the business results appendix attached to the prior-year CIT finalisation; periods under 12 months are annualised.
o: Total sales/service revenue (before deductions), financial income and other income of the immediately preceding tax year
Q4 revenue of the prior year
CIT-101.x:
Basis: Article 4(15) of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP (added by Decree 141/2026/ND-CP).
Analysis: The test uses total sales and service revenue (before deductions), financial income and other income of the prior tax year, per the business results appendix of the finalisation return; a short prior year is annualised (CIT-102).
Distractors: B uses the current year and net revenue; C and D aren't criteria.

CIT-102.q: An enterprise established in September 2025 (September counted in full) operated 4 months in 2025 with total revenue of VND 300 million. What annualised revenue is used to test the 2026 CIT exemption (VND million)?
CIT-102.e: 300 / 4 × 12 = 900 million ≤ 1 billion → eligible for the 2026 CIT exemption unless it is a subsidiary/associate of an ineligible enterprise.
CIT-102.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 300 / 4 × 12 = 900 million ≤ 1 billion → CIT-exempt in 2026 (if not a subsidiary or affiliate of an ineligible enterprise).
Note: Annualise using actual months of operation (September counted → 4 months).

CIT-103.q: A newly established enterprise expecting revenue not exceeding VND 1 billion need not make provisional CIT payments; if actual revenue exceeds VND 1 billion it declares and finalises normally without late-payment interest.
CIT-103.e: True under Decree 141/2026/ND-CP, which adds clause 15 to Article 4 of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
CIT-103.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP adding Article 4(15) of Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. New companies expecting revenue ≤ 1 billion needn't pay provisionally; if actual revenue exceeds 1 billion, they declare and finalise normally without late-payment interest for the unpaid quarters, since the forecast was reasonable.

CIT-104.q: A subsidiary with annual revenue of VND 800 million belonging to a group with revenue in the thousands of billions is still CIT-exempt under the VND 1 billion threshold.
CIT-104.e: False. The exemption does not apply to subsidiaries or associates whose related enterprise does not meet the exemption conditions.
CIT-104.x:
Basis: Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: False. As with the 15%/17% rates (CIT-023), the 1 billion exemption doesn't apply to subsidiaries or affiliates of ineligible enterprises – preventing groups from splitting to obtain exemptions.

CIT-105.q: Match the prior-year total revenue of an independent enterprise (not excluded) with its 2026 CIT treatment:
CIT-105.e: ≤ 1 billion: exempt (Decree 141/2026); ≤ 3 billion: 15%; over 3 to 50 billion: 17%; over 50 billion: 20%.
CIT-105.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Law 09/2026/QH16; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: 800 million (≤ 1 billion) → exempt; 2.5 billion (≤ 3 billion) → 15%; 20 billion (3–50 billion) → 17%; 80 billion (> 50 billion) → 20%. All based on prior-year revenue for independent enterprises.

CIT-106.q: An enterprise had total 2025 revenue of VND 2.8 billion (independent, not excluded). In 2026 accounting profit before tax is VND 420 million and non-deductible expenses VND 30 million. What is 2026 CIT (VND million)?
CIT-106.e: Rate 15%; assessable income = 420 + 30 = 450 million; CIT = 450 × 15% = 67.5 million VND.
CIT-106.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Prior-year revenue 2.8 billion (≤ 3, > 1 billion) → 15%. Taxable income = 420 + 30 = 450 million; CIT = 450 × 15% = 67.5 million VND.

CIT-107.q: A company (20% rate) in 2026: accounting profit before tax VND 3,000 million; excess welfare 80 million; depreciation of the Director's private car 60 million; deposit interest 100 million (included in profit); dividends from a domestic company 200 million; 2024 loss still available 400 million; S&T Fund appropriation of 10% of assessable income. What CIT is payable (VND million)?
CIT-107.e: Taxable income = 3,000 + 80 + 60 = 3,140 (deposit interest remains taxable). Assessable income = 3,140 − 200 − 400 = 2,540. S&T Fund = 10% × 2,540 = 254. CIT = (2,540 − 254) × 20% = 457.2 million VND.
CIT-107.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: (1) Assessable income = 3,000 + 80 (excess welfare) + 60 (personal car depreciation) = 3,140 (deposit interest stays taxable). (2) Less exempt dividends 200 and loss 400 → 2,540. (3) S&T fund 10% = 254. (4) CIT = (2,540 − 254) × 20% = 457.2 million VND.
Note: A common trap is treating deposit interest as exempt.

CIT-108.q: Which expense is NOT deductible even with full invoices and documents?
CIT-108.e: Interest corresponding to unpaid charter capital is non-deductible; the others serve the business and are deductible with valid documents.
o: Interest corresponding to charter capital the owners have not yet contributed on schedule
Warehouse rent under contract paid by transfer
CIT-108.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Interest corresponding to unpaid charter capital is specifically non-deductible, regardless of documents (CIT-048).
Distractors: B, C and D serve the business with proper records, so they're deductible.

CIT-109.q: A company borrows VND 5 billion from an associate (not a credit institution) for 6 months of 2026 at 22%/year. How much interest exceeds the Civil Code rate (before considering the related-party interest cap) (VND million)?
CIT-109.e: Interest paid = 5,000 × 22% × 6/12 = 550; maximum = 5,000 × 20% × 6/12 = 500; the 50 million excess is non-deductible. The 30% EBITDA cap under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP must also be checked.
CIT-109.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 132/2020/ND-CP (amended by Decree 20/2025/ND-CP).
Working: Interest paid = 5,000 × 22% × 6/12 = 550 million; cap = 5,000 × 20% × 6/12 = 500 million; excess = 50 million non-deductible.
Note: As a related party, net interest is also capped at 30% of EBITDA (CIT-133); both limits apply independently.

CIT-110.q: Depreciation of a fixed asset used for business but without documents proving the enterprise's ownership (other than finance leases) is not deductible.
CIT-110.e: True. The asset must be owned by the enterprise (except finance leases) and be managed and accounted for under the regime.
CIT-110.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC (fixed asset depreciation).
Analysis: True. Depreciation is deductible only for assets owned by the business (except finance leases), used in operations and accounted for properly. Assets registered to individuals (e.g., a director's car) can't be depreciated deductibly.

CIT-111.q: A company buys a 5-seat car for management (not transport or tourism) costing VND 2.4 billion, straight-line over 8 years. How much depreciation is NOT deductible each year (VND million)?
CIT-111.e: Deductible depreciation is based on a maximum cost of 1.6 billion: 1,600/8 = 200; book depreciation 2,400/8 = 300; 100 million per year is non-deductible.
CIT-111.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC.
Working: Accounting depreciation = 2,400 / 8 = 300 million/year. Deductible on the 1.6 billion cap = 1,600 / 8 = 200 million/year. Non-deductible = 100 million/year.
Note: Same logic as the input VAT cap on cars (VAT-129).

CIT-112.q: Select ALL expenses that are NOT deductible for CIT:
CIT-112.e: Unspent accruals, administrative fines and depreciation of fully depreciated assets are non-deductible; proper sponsorships and documented purchases are deductible.
o: Sponsorship for education to proper beneficiaries with confirmation documents
Purchases from a household business with invoices paid by transfer
Accrued major-repair costs not fully spent by the end of the period
Penalty for late filing of tax returns
Depreciation continued on fully depreciated fixed assets
CIT-112.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Non-deductible: (C) unspent major repair accruals (CIT-061); (D) penalties for late returns – administrative fines; (E) depreciation of fully depreciated assets – no cost left.
Distractors: (A) documented education sponsorship and (B) purchases from household businesses with invoices and transfer are deductible.

CIT-113.q: An enterprise may choose to carry losses into high-profit years within 5 years, skipping low-income years.
CIT-113.e: False. Losses must be carried forward continuously and in full to subsequent years; years cannot be skipped.
CIT-113.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15.
Analysis: False. Losses must be carried forward 'continuously and in full' against the next years' income as soon as it arises; skipping low-income years to save losses isn't allowed.

CIT-114.q: An enterprise had a 2021 tax loss of VND 900 million; 2022–2025 taxable income was 100, 150, 120 and 80 million (all offset). 2026 taxable income is 600 million. How much of the 2021 loss can still be carried into 2026 (VND million)?
CIT-114.e: The 2021 loss can be carried until 2026 (5 years: 2022–2026). Used: 100 + 150 + 120 + 80 = 450; remaining 900 − 450 = 450 million, fully offset in 2026 because income of 600 million is sufficient.
CIT-114.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15.
Working: The 2021 loss can be used over 2022–2026. Used 100 + 150 + 120 + 80 = 450; remaining 900 − 450 = 450 million. 2026 (the last year) income of 600 covers it → all 450 million used.
Note: If 2026 income were only 300, the remaining 150 million would expire.

CIT-115.q: What minimum percentage of the S&T Development Fund must be used within 5 years of appropriation to avoid tax clawback?
CIT-115.e: If the fund is unused, less than 70% is used within 5 years, or it is misused, CIT on the corresponding portion plus interest is payable.
CIT-115.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: Within 5 years of appropriation, at least 70% of the fund must be used properly; otherwise tax plus interest is due on the relevant portion (CIT-071).
Distractors: 50%, 80% and 100% aren't the prescribed level.

CIT-116.q: Finalised 2026 CIT is VND 800 million. Provisional payments over 4 quarters: 150, 150, 160 and 120 million. How much bears late-payment interest due to the shortfall against 80% (VND million)?
CIT-116.e: Paid 580; 80% × 800 = 640; the 60 million shortfall bears interest from the day after the Q4 provisional deadline.
CIT-116.x:
Basis: Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Working: Paid = 150 + 150 + 160 + 120 = 580 million. Minimum = 80% × 800 = 640 million. Interest-bearing shortfall = 60 million. The other 160 million (800 − 640) is due at finalisation.

CIT-117.q: Provisional CIT is short by VND 60,000,000; the Q4/2026 provisional deadline is 01/02/2027 (working day) and the shortfall is paid on 31/3/2027. Late days from 02/02/2027 to 30/3/2027 are 57. What is the late-payment interest (VND)?
CIT-117.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Working: 60,000,000 × 0.03% × 57 days = 1,026,000 VND.
Note: The Q4 deadline 31/01/2027 is a Sunday, so it moves to 01/02/2027; interest runs from 02/02/2027 to the day before payment (30/03/2027).

CIT-118.q: The year-end entry recognising current CIT expense payable under Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC is:
CIT-118.e: Current CIT expense: Dr 8211, Cr 3334. On payment: Dr 3334, Cr 112.
CIT-118.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC; VAS 17.
Analysis: Current tax expense: Dr 8211 / Cr 3334. On payment: Dr 3334 / Cr 112. At period-end, close 8211 to 911.
Distractors: B reverses the entry; C is a deferred tax liability; D bypasses the income statement.

CIT-119.q: An enterprise accrues VND 200 million of warranty costs in 2026 that are not yet deductible (deductible when paid). Under VAS 17 at 20%, it recognises:
CIT-119.e: Deductible temporary difference 200 million × 20% = 40 million → deferred tax asset (when future taxable profit is probable).
o: A deferred tax asset of VND 40 million (Dr 243 / Cr 8212)
A deferred tax liability of VND 40 million
An increase of current tax expense by VND 40 million
CIT-119.x:
Basis: VAS 17; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: The warranty accrual isn't deductible now but will be when paid → a 200 million deductible temporary difference. DTA = 200 × 20% = 40 million: Dr 243 / Cr 8212, provided future taxable profit is probable.
Distractors: B is for taxable differences; C ignores VAS 17; D confuses current and deferred tax.

CIT-120.q: Payables with unidentifiable creditors that the enterprise writes back to income are other income subject to CIT.
CIT-120.e: True. This is other income under CIT rules.
CIT-120.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Writing off a payable with no identifiable creditor increases net assets, so it's taxable other income.

CIT-121.q: A company (20% rate) disposes of a production line: sale price VND 700 million, tax net book value 520 million, dismantling cost with invoice 30 million. What CIT arises on this income (VND million)?
CIT-121.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15.
Working: Disposal income = 700 − 520 (tax book value) − 30 (dismantling) = 150 million; CIT = 30 million VND.
Note: Use the tax book value (after non-deductible depreciation adjustments), which may differ from the accounting value.

CIT-122.q: A bonus received from a customer for completing a contract ahead of schedule is CIT-taxable income.
CIT-122.e: True. Bonuses, compensation and penalties received are revenue or other income subject to CIT.
CIT-122.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. A customer bonus for early completion increases economic benefits – recognised as revenue (if contract-related) or other income, taxable either way. For VAT, if tied to the service, it may be part of the service price.

CIT-123.q: Select ALL income NOT eligible for a project's CIT incentives even though the enterprise enjoys incentives:
CIT-123.e: Incentives do not apply to capital transfers, real estate (except social housing) and other income not tied to the incentivised project, such as deposit interest.
o: Income from the incentivised project's own production
CIT-123.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
