Analysis: Not incentivised: (A) capital transfers; (B) commercial property transfers; (C) deposit interest – not tied to the project.
Distractors: (D) Income from the project's own production is incentivised.

CIT-124.q: An enterprise with both CIT-incentivised and non-incentivised activities must account for each activity's income separately; if it cannot, it allocates by revenue or cost ratio as prescribed.
CIT-124.e: True. Income from incentivised activities must be determined separately to apply rates and exemptions; otherwise allocate per guidance.
CIT-124.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Circular 20/2026/TT-BTC.
Analysis: True. Incentivised income must be accounted for separately to apply the right rate and reliefs. If not separable, apportion by the revenue or cost share of the incentivised activity per guidance, consistently over the years.

CIT-125.q: Under Resolution 198/2025/QH15, small and medium enterprises are CIT-exempt for how long from their first business registration?
CIT-125.e: Article 10 of Resolution 198/2025/QH15: 3-year CIT exemption for newly established SMEs.
CIT-125.x:
Basis: Article 10 of Resolution 198/2025/QH15.
Analysis: New SMEs are CIT-exempt for 3 years from their first enterprise registration certificate (CIT-097).
Distractors: 2, 4 and 5 years don't match the Resolution.

CIT-126.q: A pharmaceutical manufacturer had prior-year revenue of VND 120 billion. In 2026 accounting profit before tax is 5,000 million; qualifying R&D cost 400 million (an extra 100% deduction under Decree 320/2025, no loss after deduction); fines for late social insurance 20 million. What is CIT (VND million)?
CIT-126.e: Assessable income = 5,000 + 20 − 400 (extra deduction) = 4,620; CIT at 20% = 924 million VND.
CIT-126.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Prior-year revenue 120 billion → 20%. Taxable income = 5,000 + 20 (non-deductible social insurance penalty) − 400 (extra 100% R&D deduction) = 4,620 million; CIT = 924 million VND.
Note: The actual 400 million R&D is already in accounting profit; only the extra portion is deducted.

CIT-127.q: Which income tax does an individual household business pay?
CIT-127.e: Household/individual businesses pay PIT (and VAT), not CIT.
CIT-127.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; PIT Law 109/2025/QH15.
Analysis: Household and individual businesses aren't enterprises, so they aren't CIT taxpayers; their business income is subject to PIT (and VAT above the threshold).
Distractors: B confuses the entity type; C is wrong above the threshold; D – contractor tax is for foreign parties.

CIT-128.e: Exemption ≤ 1 billion; the interest cap is 20%/year under the Civil Code; provisional payment due on the last day of the first month of the next quarter; 17% for 3–50 billion.
o: An independent enterprise with prior-year revenue of VND 900 million is CIT-exempt.
The cap on individual-loan interest is 150% of the base rate.
Quarterly provisional CIT is due on the last day of the first month of the next quarter.
The 17% rate applies when prior-year revenue is over VND 3 billion up to 50 billion.
CIT-128.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15; Decree 141/2026/ND-CP; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: (1) True – 900 million ≤ 1 billion, exempt. (2) False – the cap is 20%/year under the Civil Code (150% of the base rate was the old rule). (3) True – quarterly payments are due by the last day of the next quarter's first month. (4) True – 17% for prior-year revenue above 3 up to 50 billion.

CIT-129.q: Arrange the annual CIT finalisation workflow:
CIT-129.e: Workflow: accounting figures → tax adjustments → return → reconcile provisional payments → file and pay on time.
o: Close the books and prepare annual financial statements
Review non-deductible expenses, exempt income, losses carried forward
Prepare the finalisation return and appendices
Reconcile provisional payments to determine any extra payment or overpayment
File and pay by the last day of the third month after year-end
CIT-129.x:
Basis: Law 108/2025/QH15; Decree 252/2026/ND-CP.
Analysis: Sequence: close the books and prepare FS → review tax adjustments (non-deductibles, exempt income, losses) → prepare the return and appendices → reconcile provisional payments → file and pay by the last day of the third month after year-end.
Note: Check the 80% provisional threshold before closing Q4 to limit interest.

CIT-130.q: Contributions to voluntary pension insurance and life insurance for employees are deductible within the prescribed cap and must be stated in the labour contract, collective labour agreement or company regulations.
CIT-130.e: True. The usual cap is no more than VND 3 million per person per month; conditions and benefit levels must be specified in valid internal documents.
CIT-130.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Analysis: True. Supplementary pension and life insurance for employees are deductible within the cap (commonly 3 million VND/month/person) and must be set out in employment contracts, collective agreements or policies. Consider the employees' PIT treatment too.

CIT-131.q: A company pays voluntary pension insurance for 20 employees at VND 4 million per person per month for 12 months (with internal rules). How much is NOT deductible (above VND 3 million per person per month) (VND million)?
CIT-131.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.
Working: Excess = (4 − 3) million × 20 people × 12 months = 240 million non-deductible. Deductible = 3 × 20 × 12 = 720 million.

CIT-132.q: CIT revenue from construction and installation is:
CIT-132.e: Construction revenue is the value of works, items or completed volume accepted.
o: The value of the works, items or accepted construction volume
CIT-132.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP.

CIT-133.q: An enterprise with related-party transactions has 2026 EBITDA of VND 10 billion; total interest expense net of deposit and lending interest is VND 4 billion. Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, how much interest is non-deductible this year (carried forward) (VND billion)?
CIT-133.e: Maximum deductible = 30% × 10 = 3 billion; the excess 4 − 3 = 1 billion is not deductible this year and is carried forward (up to 5 years) as prescribed.
CIT-133.x:
Basis: Decree 132/2020/ND-CP (amended by Decree 20/2025/ND-CP) on related-party transactions.
Working: Cap = 30% × EBITDA 10 billion = 3 billion. Net interest 4 billion → 1 billion excess is non-deductible this year and carried forward (up to 5 years) when later net interest is below the 30% cap.
Note: The cap applies to total net interest (after deposit and lending interest), not only related-party interest.

CIT-134.q: The CIT rate for an independent enterprise with prior-year total revenue of exactly VND 3 billion is:
CIT-134.e: 15% applies to total annual revenue not exceeding VND 3 billion (including exactly 3 billion).
CIT-134.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15.
Analysis: 15% applies to annual revenue 'not exceeding 3 billion' – including exactly 3 billion. No exemption since revenue exceeds 1 billion.
Distractors: B – 17% is for 'above 3 billion'; C – 20% above 50 billion; D – exemption only if ≤ 1 billion.

CIT-135.q: Rent paid to an individual lessor under a lease contract with payment documents is deductible; if the contract has the enterprise pay tax on the individual's behalf, the tax paid on behalf is also deductible.
CIT-135.e: True. Rent paid to individuals with full documentation (and tax paid on their behalf by agreement) is deductible.
CIT-135.x:
Basis: Decree 320/2025/ND-CP; Decree 68/2026/ND-CP (tax on individuals leasing assets).
Analysis: True. Rent paid to individuals is deductible with a lease and payment records. If the lease says the company pays the individual's taxes (VAT, PIT), that tax is part of the rent cost and also deductible.

CIT-136.q: Under VAS 17, a taxable temporary difference (e.g., tax depreciation faster than book depreciation) gives rise to:
CIT-136.e: Taxable temporary differences increase future taxable income → recognise a deferred tax liability.
o: An immediate increase in current CIT payable
CIT-136.x:
Basis: VAS 17; Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Faster tax depreciation means lower taxable income now and higher later as it reverses → a taxable temporary difference → deferred tax liability (account 347).
Distractors: B is for deductible differences (CIT-119); C is the reverse; D confuses it with a permanent difference.

CIT-137.q: An enterprise with prior-year total revenue of VND 60 billion has 2026 assessable income of VND 1,250 million. What CIT is payable (VND million)?
CIT-137.x:
Basis: CIT Law 67/2025/QH15 (rates by revenue size – per the question).
Working: Prior-year revenue of 60 billion (> 50 billion) → the standard 20% rate: tax = 1,250 × 20% = 250 million VND.
Analysis: Law 67/2025 sets concessional rates for small firms: revenue up to 3 billion: 15%; above 3 to 50 billion: 17%; above 50 billion: 20%. The test uses the immediately preceding year's total revenue.
Note: Check guidance on determining prior-year revenue (new firms, related groups).

CIT-138.q: Interest on green bonds is CIT-exempt income under Law 67/2025/QH15.
CIT-138.e: True. Law 67/2025/QH15 exempts green bond interest and the first transfer of green bonds.
CIT-138.x:
Basis: Article 4 of Law 67/2025/QH15.
Analysis: True. Green bond interest and income from their first transfer after issuance are exempt – an incentive to channel capital into green projects (CIT-036).

CIT-139.q: Enterprise A (prior-year revenue VND 2 billion, independent) has a 100 million loss from its main business but 500 million income from a real-estate transfer in 2026, and chooses to offset. CIT payable is:
CIT-139.e: Law 67/2025/QH15 allows offsetting business losses against real-estate transfer income: (500 − 100) × 15% = 60 million VND (15% because prior-year revenue ≤ 3 billion).
CIT-139.x:
Basis: Law 67/2025/QH15 (offsetting losses against property transfer income); Article 10 of Law 67/2025.
Working: Offset: 500 − 100 = 400 million. Prior-year revenue 2 billion (≤ 3 billion, independent) → 15% per the key: 400 × 15% = 60 million VND.
Distractors: B ignores the offset; C uses the wrong size-based rate; D ignores the transfer income.
Note: In practice, check Decree 320/2025 on which income types qualify for the 15%/17% rates (some may be excluded).
